title: Jorgensen 2005: centroid distance of rectus abdominis at L5-S1 (F, standing)

imaging.modality: MRI 0.6 T FONAR positional (upright) open MRI, T1 axial (TR 870, TE 140)
imaging.plane: axial slices PARALLEL to and through the approximate centre of each lumbar disc (L1/L2..L5/S1)
imaging.posture_detail: standing upright neutral, no hand load, retaining bar across abdomen

quantity.name: centroid_distance
quantity.definition: distance from the vertebral-body (or disc) centroid to the muscle area centroid in the image plane; AP signed (+ anterior, - posterior), ML unsigned lateral distance. NOT a true moment arm; distance corrected from the disc-parallel scan plane to the transverse plane (Fig. 2)

source.authors: Jorgensen MJ, Marras WS, Smith FW, Pope MH
source.sample: 5 females; healthy female volunteers from an existing upright-MRI study

protocol.summary: Upright standing MRI; sagittal distance between disc centroid and rectus abdominis centroid.
how_to_simulate: Put the model in upright neutral standing (no hand load).
Locate the L5-S1 disc centroid; take the PCSA-weighted centroid of each rectus abdominis where its path crosses the plane through that disc centre (disc-parallel plane).
Project the disc-centroid -> muscle-centroid vector onto the horizontal (transverse) plane and report its AP component (+ anterior).
Compare right and left separately (or average); this is a centroid distance, not a moment arm.

subject_model.source: Methods: stature range 162.6-177.8 cm, body mass range 49.9-68.0 kg (means not given)

protocol.notes: Authors call these sagittal plane moment arms. Only 5 subjects. Table 2 also lists literature (supine) values (Jorgensen 2001, Chaffin 1990, Kumar 1988, Nemeth & Ohlsen 1986) - not stored here (other studies).

extraction.check_notes: All values verified on rendered page 244; Table 1 vs Table 2 inconsistency at right L4/L5 (8.6 vs 8.7) noted.
